problem: Prior LLM-based navigation work (e.g., VELMA, LM-Nav) only optimizes nominal performance and ignores security; the vulnerability of LLM reasoning in outdoor urban navigation to adversarial prompt perturbations is unexplored.
motivation: LLM navigators are moving toward real-world uses (driving, logistics, rescue), and LLMs are known to be highly sensitive to input variations. A small change to the instruction can send the agent to wrong actions, so the risk must be measured and mitigated.
key_idea: Perturb the navigation prompt with gradient-searched adversarial affixes (NPI: insert; NPS: swap one important word) to derail LLM navigators, and defend by re-prompting with reasoning-oriented prompt engineering (NPE).
insight: Affixes found on LLaMa/Vicuna transfer to GPT-3/GPT-4 and LM-Nav, so the fragility is shared across LLMs, and LLaMa-derived affixes are stronger than Vicuna's. NPS attacks on intersection words hurt more than on landmark words (e.g., Map2seq VELMA-FT TC 38.5→17.5 vs 32.0). Simple prompt-engineering defenses recover a lot (role-play best), but do not fully restore performance; the adversarial-training baseline helps little.
method: NPI attack: append an adversarial affix to the prompt x_t; token substitutions are chosen from the top-k negative gradients w.r.t. one-hot token indicators, random candidate subset sampled, and the token minimizing -log P(a_t|x) is kept (GCG-like).
NPS attack: compute word importance as gradient magnitude, swap the single most important word (targeting intersection or landmark descriptions) with a vocabulary token that minimizes the loss.
White/black-box protocol: affixes optimized on LLaMa or Vicuna; applying to a LLaMa-based navigator is white-box, applying to other LLMs (GPT-3/4, LLaMa2, etc.) is black-box.
Target model: VELMA variants (GPT-3.5, GPT-4 Turbo, LLaMa, LLaMa2 with 2-shot ICL; LLaMa-7B fine-tuned FT and RBL) on Touchdown and Map2seq; also LM-Nav.
New metrics: SPD, KPA, TC, TC-1, FKPE, DI (danger impact), PL.
NPE defense: rewrite the prompt via f_NPE using zero-shot CoT, Plan-and-Solve, or Role-Play prompting to focus on navigation-relevant keywords, with no retraining.
Comparisons: Zou et al. universal suffix adapted as attack baseline; adversarial training and adaptive system prompt (ASP) as defense baselines.

setting.backbone: VELMA with GPT-3.5 Turbo / GPT-4 Turbo (frozen, 2-shot), LLaMa-7B / LLaMa2 (2-shot), LLaMa-7B fine-tuned (FT, RBL); CLIP for landmark scoring; LM-Nav (GPT-3 + CLIP + ViNG)
setting.model_size: LLaMa-7B for FT/RBL; GPT-3.5 (~175B) and GPT-4 Turbo as described
setting.training_data: Attack: gradient-based affix optimization on LLaMa/Vicuna; navigators use original VELMA training (FT/RBL on full Touchdown/Map2seq training sets); the defense is training-free (adversarial training baseline retrains on adversarial prompts)
setting.observation: Street-view 360° panoramas converted to text (landmark verbalization via CLIP) plus instruction text
setting.action_space: discrete: forward, left, right, turn_around, stop on street-view graph
setting.simulator: Touchdown / Map2seq street-view graph environments (Google Street View, Manhattan)
setting.privileged: White-box attacks use gradient access to the LLM; otherwise none

numbers_note: These are attack/defense results, not navigation SOTA. Many more variants (GPT-3/4, LLaMa, LLaMa2, FT, NPS) appear in the tables; only representative rows are listed. Split named 'val-unseen' per the table captions ('unseen scenario').
results: NPI/NPS attacks degrade all seven metrics on Touchdown and Map2seq for all VELMA variants, e.g., Map2seq VELMA-FT SPD 9.6→20.0 and FKPE 62→155 (+150%), and LM-Nav success 0.8→0.1. The NPI attack beats an adapted Zou et al. suffix baseline (VELMA-FT TC 38.5→3.8 vs 18.2). NPE-RP restores VELMA-RBL Map2seq TC from 11.4 to 29.0, comparable to ASP and far above adversarial training.
limitations: Defenses are only partial and don't restore clean performance, especially for 2-shot LLaMa models and on Touchdown
Costly evaluation (GPT-4 only on Touchdown) and only VELMA and LM-Nav tested; attacks target the text prompt only, with no real-robot tests
Impact of the attack depends on affix source and insertion; the NPS comparison to defenses used inconsistent naming (NPS/NPI)
builds_on: Zou et al. universal adversarial suffix (GCG)
compares_to: Zou et al. universal suffix attack
